failure_modes.claim: "The label is sung aloud" — caused by the cue being too verbose or too lyrical. Remedy: keep bracket cues short.
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — Suno Meta Tags Guide 2026

failure_modes.claim: 'Avoid tag stuffing. A long bracket inventory makes the map harder to read.' Recommends testing one variable at a time; 'Every retry is unrelated' results from changing too many variables at once.
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — Suno Meta Tags Guide 2026

failure_modes.claim: CRITICAL: 'parentheses are ALWAYS sung. Don't put performance instructions in them — (whispered) will be sung as the word "whispered."' This directly contradicts sunoaiwiki's advice to use parentheses for spoken delivery.
failure_modes.source_label: SongSmith — Lyric Formatting Symbols Cheat Sheet

failure_modes.claim: Square brackets are the opposite of parentheses: 'Anything inside [ ] is a structural or production cue. Suno reads it and acts on it but doesn't sing it.'
failure_modes.source_label: SongSmith — Lyric Formatting Symbols Cheat Sheet

failure_modes.claim: 'Quotation marks work better for spoken effects than tags like [Spoken Word]. The tag changes a whole section. Quotes change one phrase.' — scope mismatch is itself a failure mode.
failure_modes.source_label: SongSmith — Lyric Formatting Symbols Cheat Sheet

failure_modes.claim: 'Tags being sung as lyrics' occurs when tags aren't on their own line; 'Song ignores structure tags' happens with complex tag descriptions; 'Parenthetical directions being sung' results from full sentences in parentheses.
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Suno Lyrics Formatting

failure_modes.claim: Rhyme, repeated hooks, chorus labels and melodic Style terms all encourage SINGING — the main obstacle to spoken output. Also: stage directions get interpreted as lyrics; music bed too active masks the voice; too many words causes rushed delivery.
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — How to Make Suno Speak Instead of Sing

failure_modes.claim: Speech is not a guaranteed mode: 'Suno is built around music generation, so speech is a creative performance tendency—not a guaranteed narration mode.' Suno publishes no official spoken-narration syntax.
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — How to Make Suno Speak Instead of Sing

failure_modes.claim: Using [Verse]/[Chorus]/[Bridge] on a narration piece 'Forced pop song behavior'; 'lullaby ballad'/'dreamy sung story' 'Triggered melody-based phrasing'; '#Structure: Verse-Chorus-Bridge' 'Conflicted with narrative flow'; even the phrase 'sung narration' 'Still produced melodic lines'.
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — When the World Was a Whisper

failure_modes.claim: Duet collapse: 'If a song keeps collapsing into one singer, swapping male and female lines, or reading behavior cues inconsistently, the issue is usually one of three things: speaker labels are too weak, sections are too long, or the overlap is too ambitious.' Labeling only once at the top is insufficient.
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — Duet & Harmony Meta Tags

failure_modes.claim: 'It reads tags/objects as lyrics' when there is 'non-lyric text in lyrics field; bracket noise'. Fix: 'Keep lyric field as singable text only.'
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — Duet & Harmony Meta Tags

failure_modes.claim: CONTRADICTION BETWEEN FIELDS: 'If the style prompt says "breathy female" and the lyrics say [Male Vocal] [Aggressive], Suno picks one and you don't know which. When both fields agree, compliance is highest.' — 'Reinforce, don't contradict.'
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Suno Vocal Prompts: What Works, What's Placebo

failure_modes.claim: Long bracket cues degrade: 'The model's tokenizer front-loads processing and prefers short, recognizable descriptors. Long bracketed sentences like [Ethereal synth build with rising tension over sparse percussion] get compressed into noise.' Keep each tag to 1-3 words.
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Suno Vocal Prompts: What Works, What's Placebo

failure_modes.claim: Mid-song gender swaps WITHOUT per-line [Male]/[Female] labels are 'Tier 3' reliability — 'the model can't anchor the switch.' Precise register words collapse to ~30-50% when 'stranded in a bracket with no reinforcement'.
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Suno Vocal Prompts: What Works, What's Placebo

failure_modes.claim: Colon+number parameter tags are PLACEBO: '[Reverb: 30%], [Bass: 80%] ... Suno ignores them completely.' Reason given: 'The syntax feels official — square brackets, colons, numbers — and the first guide to invent it got copied into the next guide.' Relevant caution for the [Vocal Style: X] colon family.
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Suno Vocal Prompts: What Works, What's Placebo

failure_modes.claim: Tier ranking (from a claimed 400+ generation test): gender, delivery mode (whisper, rap, belt, spoken word), BPM and basic texture (raspy, breathy) are Tier-1 reliably honored; [Whispered] is '>80% compliance'; [Spoken Word] is 'Tier 1 and one of the cleanest-complying tags Suno has'. [Falsetto] ~60%. [Intro] 'notoriously skipped entirely'.
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Suno Vocal Prompts: What Works, What's Placebo

failure_modes.claim: VOICES/PERSONA OVERRIDE: when the Voices (clone) feature is active you should drop the gender descriptor from the style prompt — 'the clone already carries it, and stacking a conflicting gender cue makes the output smear.'
failure_modes.source_label: Jack Righteous — How to Change the Voice in Suno (via search excerpt; page itself not directly fetched)

failure_modes.claim: Omitting gender entirely causes random male/female selection — 'the root cause of roughly every "why does Suno keep changing the voice" complaint.' Also 'Conflicting vocal descriptors' such as 'soft powerful vocals' are contradictory — pick one direction.
failure_modes.source_label: HookGenius — Fix Suno Bad Vocals

failure_modes.claim: Placement: 'Tags go before the lyrics / Never mid-line'. Contradictory stacks explicitly shown as wrong: '[Chorus | aggressive | calm | minimal | maximal | orchestral | techno | acoustic]'. Meta tags 'guide, they don't command' — cannot force exact melodies or override Suno's rules.
failure_modes.source_label: Stoke McToke — The Complete Suno AI Meta Tags Guide

failure_modes.claim: Chorus modifiers are frequently NOT honored: 'the Chirp system decides how to render the chorus, so modifiers are often NOT honored'. Also 'The system seems to ignore capitalization' — relevant to the casing question. Note this source predates v5.
failure_modes.source_label: github daveshap/suno README

failure_modes.claim: Duets are unreliable in principle: 'metatags within the lyrics might assign multiple voices, but the gender and consistency are not reliable'; voices swap roles or come out too similar; 'duets are more of an exploit, definitely not a feature.'
failure_modes.source_label: Suno.wiki — Are Duets Possible? (via search excerpt; page returned 403 on direct fetch)

failure_modes.claim: Style-field vs bracket SCOPE difference: 'Putting whispered in the Style field makes the entire song whispered. Putting [whispered] in a bracket tag before Verse 2 makes only that section whispered.' Misplacing the cue is a scope failure.
failure_modes.source_label: AceTagGen — SUNO Vocal Tricks

failure_modes.claim: ALL CAPS is a LOUDNESS control, not a speaker label: 'Words in ALL CAPS get sung with more force. Use sparingly — 1 to 3 words max per section, otherwise Suno averages and the effect disappears.' A line that is all caps 'becomes a shout'. This is evidence AGAINST bare ALL-CAPS text functioning as a narrator attribution.
failure_modes.source_label: SongSmith — Lyric Formatting Symbols Cheat Sheet

failure_modes.claim: Metatags work best 'when they are short, often just one or two words, maybe up to three'; the AI 'generates voices randomly, so this takes trial and error'; [Intro] is 'less reliable in Suno'.
failure_modes.source_label: TitanXT — Metatags Explained

notes: METHOD CONFIRMATION: the bracket-only-regex hazard is real and was avoided. Two of the highest-value sources list tags with NO brackets at all — sunoaiwiki.com/resources (Female narrator, Announcer, Reporter, Man, Woman, Whispers all plain text with ' : ' glosses) and stokemctoke.com (Narrator, Spoken word, Whispered vocals, Chant as bare lines). A bracket regex would have returned ZERO from both.

However, correcting the brief's expectation: the sunoaiwiki *List of Metatags* page is NOT unusually dense. Full raw HTML is 49KB but only ~5.5KB of text / 116 lines total, and it yields just 9 in-lane entries. Its density claim did not hold up on direct read. The dense spoken-word material on that domain is on the separate /tips/ page, which contributed the 4-tag set [Spoken word]/[Narration]/[Spoken verse]/[Sprechgesang].

INFLATION CONFIRMED, as warned. openmusicprompt.com advertises '500+ Verified Metatags' but the page yields only 118 unique bracket forms total across ALL categories. sunometatagcreator.com advertises '1000+ Tags' but yields 231 unique bracket forms and only ~6 in-lane hits. Both counts include structure/instrument/mood tags, so the in-lane fraction is tiny.

SPARSE-EVIDENCE WARNING on the brief's example forms. Several syntaxes named in the task spec were NOT found verbatim in any source I actually read: '[Verse 1, Man]' (comma-separated speaker inside a section bracket), '[Outro, Tay Chatbot:]', '[Monster spoken, raspy, angry]', '[Female spoken, vocaloid, gentle]', '[narrator: voice: female, style: documentary]' (nested double-colon), '[spoken word | intimate, close-mic]', '[Male: gritty baritone]', '(Voice A)'/'(Voice B)', '[VOICEOVER — SPOKEN, NOT SUNG]', '[PERFORMANCE RULES]', bare 'FEMALE NARRATOR:' and 'WHISPERS:'. Per rule 4 this is NOT evidence they do not exist — the likely habitats (Reddit, Facebook groups, the suno.com song pages, the paywalled howtopromptsuno tiers, YouTube descriptions) were exactly the sources that were blocked. I did not invent them.

What I DID find are structural cousins of each: the pipe form exists but as [Verse | spoken word | low energy] (stokemctoke) not with a leading bare 'spoken word'; the colon form exists as [Vocal Style: Whisper] and [Verse: whispered, intimate]; the gender-prefix form exists as [Female Narrator] and [Ethereal Female Whisper]; the em-dash rule-block form exists as [Creation Begins — voice softens]; character-name-in-bracket has its closest analogue in daveshap's persona tags [Female Opera Singer] / [Swanky Crooning Male] / [Opera Female Pre-Chorus].

ONE A_demo ONLY. https://suno.com/s/p0DaHm06qIJicA3U (linked from the jackrighteous 'When the World Was a Whisper' case study) is the sole publicly playable link I saw tied to specific spoken-word cue syntax. I did not play the audio; I graded A_demo because the source links a playable suno.com/s/ URL for the exact prompt shown, per the grading rule. Everything else is B_recited.

DIRECT SOURCE CONFLICT worth flagging for downstream use: sunoaiwiki says parentheses trigger SPOKEN delivery; songsmith.studio says parentheses are ALWAYS SUNG and '(whispered)' will be sung as the literal word 'whispered'. Both are recited claims with no demo. Also conflicting: hookgenius shows [Whispered] inline at the head of a lyric line, while its own sibling page says tags sung as lyrics happen when 'tags aren't on their own line'.

CASING IS GENUINELY UNSTABLE ACROSS SOURCES and was preserved rather than normalized: [Spoken Word] / [Spoken word] / [spoken word] / [SPOKEN WORD-absent], [Whispered] / [whispered] / [Whispers] / [whispers], [Female Narrator] / [female narrator] / 'Female narrator'. daveshap notes 'The system seems to ignore capitalization', which if true means these are one token family, but that is a single unverified claim.

OFFICIAL DOCS ARE EMPTY ON THIS LANE — a substantive negative finding, and this one IS from pages I actually read. help.suno.com article 9010177 (Music Glossary) has no entry for spoken word, narration, sprechgesang, whisper, chant, recitative or monologue; only 'Rapping — Rhythmic spoken or chanted lyrics'. help.suno.com article 5782977 (V4.5 Better Prompts in Lyrics) contains no bracket examples at all. Every spoken/narrator tag in this inventory is community-sourced, not vendor-documented.

The 'Bark lineage' cluster is worth noting for provenance: sunoprompt.com attributes [announcer]/[female narrator]/[reporter]/[whispers]/[man]/[woman]/[clears throat] to the Bark model section, and these are the same tokens sunoaiwiki lists unbracketed. This suggests one shared upstream origin (Suno's Bark TTS ancestry) rather than independent confirmation — several sources in this inventory are likely copies of each other, not corroboration.

extracted_count counts distinct (tag, source) pairs in `tags` (74) plus distinct entries in `speaker_syntax` (25) = 99. Duplicate tag strings from different sources are counted separately because casing/bracketing differed or the gloss differed.
